title: Hedged routing policy and soft-shed controller for multi-region inference
creator: Ethan Clarke
description: Goal: implement a composable policy that balances latency SLOs, per-region capacity signals, and application affinity (geo-pinning) with graceful degradation. Deliver a controller that can: 1) compute a per-request routing decision based on latency budget, region capacity score, and pinning hints; 2) apply a soft-shed (probabilistic drop + hedging) mechanism when capacity headroom is low; 3) expose circuit-breaker state per-region and per-model variant for operator visibility and automated failover. This ticket covers design, implementation, canary rollout, and chaos validation for the new policy engine and the soft-shed controller. Out of scope: persistent per-customer rate-limits and billing integration (tracked in other tickets).
acceptance_criteria: New routing policy implemented as pluggable module behind existing request director API
Latency SLO enforcement: for test workload, p95 tail remains within 15% of baseline under 80% global load; p99 degrades gracefully with hedging enabled
Circuit-breaker trips and recovers according to configured windows (open >= 30s when sustained overload, half-open probe succeeds before transitioning)
Soft-shed controller reduces offered load by probabilistic drop to keep region CPU/GPU utilization under soft limit and logs sampled dropped requests for postmortem
Geo-pinning respected for pinned customers unless explicit overrule (emergency override) is enabled
Operator dashboard surfaces per-region capacity score, circuit state, hedging rate, and dropped request rate
Automated chaos runs (latency spike, blackhole region, CPU pressure) show no customer-visible error-rate spike > 2x baseline for canary traffic group

comments: 2026-02-02 Ethan Clarke: Initial ticket created after sync with product. Motivation: recent multi-region incidents where overloaded regions caused cascading latency spikes. We need a policy that blends latency budgets, capacity signals, and pinning without hard ejects.

2026-02-08 Riya Patel: Posted design draft: /confluence/routing/hedged-policy-2026. Key idea: compute a region_score = alpha * (1 - normalized_latency) + beta * capacity_headroom - gamma * cross_region_cost. Routing decision uses soft thresholds to start hedging before full circuit trips.

2026-02-14 Jamal Ortiz: Observability proposal uploaded. We'll add metrics: region_capacity_score, circuit_state{open,half-open,closed}, hedging_rate, shed_rate. Need to pin request IDs for sampled dropped requests for investigation.

2026-02-21 Mateo Singh: Prototype routing module implemented. Early perf numbers: single-region baseline p95=110ms, p99=300ms. Under load with hedging off, failing region sees p95=220ms; with hedging at 20% we push p95 back to 140ms while offloading to healthy regions. Will push PR for review.
2026-02-25 PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842 - initial hedged-router. Requesting review from infra and runtime leads.
2026-03-03 Review (Sofia Martinez): UX notes - add a toggle to force geo-pin override for support flows. Also request retention policy for dropped request traces (7 days).

2026-03-05 QA (Priya Nair): Chaos run 1 results attached. Blackhole region B: canary traffic with hedging at 25% saw 0.8% increase in 5xx vs baseline, global p95 increased by 6%. Meets initial SLO targets. Need longer-duration run and tuning for lower-cost models.

2026-03-10 Riya Patel: Decision made to use a two-tier circuit-breaker: soft circuit (probabilistic shed + hedging ramp) and hard circuit (stop routing to region after sustained overload). Config knobs: soft_shed_threshold(0.7), soft_shed_max(0.4), hard_open_threshold(0.9), hard_open_window(30s), half_open_probe_rate(5%)
2026-03-10 Ethan Clarke: Assigned follow-ups: dashboard alerts (Sofia), canary rollout plan (Priya), add per-customer pin-exemption allowlist (security review required later).
notes: Design tradeoffs: we prefer gradual probabilistic shedding to abrupt ejection to avoid cache stampedes and to preserve KV cache locality. Hedging rate should be tuned per-model and per-region; cheaper models can be hedged more aggressively. We will default to conservative alpha/beta values and surface a tuning guide. Operationally, hard circuit opens only after operator-configured sustained high loss or resource pressure to avoid flapping.
telemetry_workflow: Emit events: routing.decision.{chosen_region,alt_regions}, routing.score.{per_region}, controller.action.{hedge,drop,open,close,probe}. Hook into existing SLO alerting: slo.router.p95 and slo.router.p99, and add slo.router.dropped_rate for regression detection.
